tour.name: Mount Batur Private Sunrise Trek: Breakfast on the Volcano & Natural Hot Springs
tour.subtitle: A private night-to-morning adventure with a licensed mountain guide and car: the climb by torchlight up Bali's active volcano, sunrise over Mount Agung and Lake Batur from the crater rim, breakfast cooked in volcanic steam, the steaming vents of the crater and a soak in hot springs by the lake.

highlights: A private guided climb of Mount Batur by torchlight

A soak in natural hot springs by the lake
Private car and licensed mountain guide
tour.overview:
Mount Batur, 1,717 metres high, is an active volcano that rises from a vast caldera in north-east Bali, beside a crescent-shaped crater lake. It last erupted in 2000, and black lava flows from the eruptions of the 1960s still scar its flanks. The Batur caldera is part of a UNESCO Global Geopark, and its sunrise view – the sun rising behind the sacred Mount Agung, with Lombok's Mount Rinjani on the horizon – is one of the best experiences in Bali.

This private trek takes you up in the dark with a licensed mountain guide, so you reach the summit for sunrise. After breakfast cooked in the volcano's steam, you walk around the crater rim, descend through the forest and lava fields and soak in hot springs by the lake.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 10 hours (2:00 to noon)
• Start and end: your hotel in Bali
• Type: private trek with licensed mountain guide, private car and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: moderate to hard; about 2 hours up on steep volcanic gravel, 600 metres of climb

WHAT YOU SEE
• The night sky over the caldera.
• Sunrise over Mount Agung and Lake Batur.
• The crater rim and steam vents.
• The lava fields.
• The hot springs of Toya Bungkah.

WHY THIS WORKS
A private guide lets you walk at your own pace, with no rush, and choose the quieter crater-rim route after sunrise.

WHO IT SUITS
Reasonably fit walkers, families with teenagers and anyone who loves sunrises.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you prefer an easy day, choose our Ubud or sea temples tours; you can also see Batur from the Kintamani viewpoints without climbing.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Pick-up is between 2:00 and 3:00 depending on your hotel. It is cold at the top before dawn: bring a warm layer. The climb is on loose gravel and steep in places; good shoes are essential.

days.name: The night climb of Mount Batur, sunrise and breakfast on the summit, the crater rim and hot springs
days.description:
What to expect: Bali's volcano at dawn with a private mountain guide, private car, permit, breakfast and hot springs.

Your driver collects you at your hotel between 2:00 and 3:00, depending on where you stay, and drives you up into the mountains. At the trailhead at about 4:00, you meet your licensed mountain guide, who gives you a torch and explains the route. You climb through the forest and then up open slopes of volcanic sand and gravel, under the stars, for about two hours, with rests whenever you need them.

You reach the summit, at 1,717 metres, before dawn. As the sky lightens, the caldera appears below you: the crescent of Lake Batur, the villages on its shore and, to the east, the perfect cone of Mount Agung, Bali's highest and holiest mountain, with Mount Rinjani on the island of Lombok beyond. Your guide prepares breakfast, cooking eggs and bananas in the steam that rises from cracks in the rock, served with bread and hot tea or coffee, while monkeys watch from nearby.

After sunrise you walk part of the crater rim, past steaming vents and craters formed in the eruptions of 1963, 1974 and 2000, and descend by a different path through the black lava fields. Your driver meets you at the bottom and takes you to a natural hot spring on the shore of Lake Batur, where you soak your muscles in warm mineral pools with a view of the volcano you have just climbed. You are back at your hotel at about 12:00.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
02:00 – Pick-up at your hotel (time depends on location).
04:00 – Start of the trek.
06:00 – Sunrise and breakfast on the summit.
07:30 – Crater rim and steam vents.
08:30 – Descent through the lava fields.
09:30 – Hot springs by Lake Batur.
10:30 – Drive back.
12:00 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• A coffee plantation stop on the way back can be added.
• The trek can be cancelled by the authorities if volcanic activity increases.
• Cloud sometimes hides the sunrise; the mountain is still wonderful.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed mountain guide, permit and torches, breakfast, hot springs entrance, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: breakfast.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: How hard is the climb?
faq.answer: About 2 hours up and 1 hour 30 minutes down, with 600 metres of climb on loose gravel. Fit beginners can do it at their own pace with a private guide.

faq.question: What is the minimum age?
faq.answer: We recommend at least 10 years old, with children used to walking.

faq.question: Is breakfast included?
faq.answer: Yes, cooked on the summit in volcanic steam, with tea or coffee.

faq.question: Will we see the sunrise?
faq.answer: Most mornings from April to October are clear. Clouds can hide the view, especially in the rainy season.

faq.question: Is it cold at the top?
faq.answer: Yes, often around 10 to 15 °C before dawn, and windy. Bring a warm layer; jackets can be rented on site.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: No. The trail is steep and uneven. The Kintamani viewpoints offer views of the volcano without climbing.

faq.question: Are the hot springs included?
faq.answer: Yes, entrance to a natural hot spring by Lake Batur. Bring a swimsuit and towel.

faq.question: Will we be taken to shops?
faq.answer: No. There are no commission stops.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tips are appreciated in Bali, especially for the mountain guide, but never required.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Trainers or hiking shoes with good grip, warm layers, a light rain jacket, and a swimsuit for the hot springs.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: April to October for clear skies. In the rainy season the trail is slippery and sunrises often cloudy.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour, and at no cost if the authorities close the mountain. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
